question: Can objects/research/Mission carry a CMOS mission, as the Sprint 203 memo assumed?
answer: No. Four independent blockers, each measured against the live store.

blockers.detail: CMOS mission statuses vs the object's declared enum
blockers.note: Dropped and Deferred have no counterpart in the research state set at all; the other three differ in case and spacing, and the object's own field description forbids coercing an unknown value ("The API remains authoritative; do not coerce an unknown server value").

blockers.detail: research/Mission declares id as a uuid with format uuid
blockers.note: Not one CMOS mission id is a uuid; they are slugs such as s203-m06.

blockers.detail: research/Mission declares project_id as a uuid

blockers.note: materialization_pending and search_ready are TraceLab pipeline internals; a CMOS mission has no value for either.

shape.note: sprint_id is the link that organises the whole of CMOS and research/Mission has nowhere to put it.

governance: objects/research/Mission.object.yaml is TraceLab-owned (metadata.owners: TraceLab) and its README states the YAML "does not add columns to TraceLab". Widening its enum or adding CMOS columns would edit another team's object to fit ours.
registry: The object registry is keyed by name (Map<string, ObjectDefinition>), so a second object named Mission cannot exist beside it either.
conclusion: research/Mission is TraceLab's research job, not a delivery mission that happens to look like it. The reuse is refused on measurement, and this sprint authors Decision, Sprint and Session only; a CMOS mission reaches these screens as Sprint's derived mission_count and as the mission_id a Decision names. Authoring a competing Mission object is out of scope: no screen in this sprint needs one.
